Partition every size-n object by a first, last, or distinguished feature. If the cases are exhaustive and disjoint, their counts add to a recurrence.
A reliable modeling workflow is: define the state, choose a reversible case split, translate each case to a smaller state, and supply enough initial values to start the recurrence.
This recurrence counts length-n boards tiled by squares and dominoes: classify by the final tile.

items.text: The cases must be mutually exclusive and cover every object exactly once.
Each reduction must be reversible; otherwise smaller objects may have the wrong multiplicity.
Initial conditions include empty objects when they make concatenation or recurrence boundaries uniform.
If the last choice depends on earlier choices, enlarge the state rather than pretending independence.
